name: Common UI Field Guide
note: Definitions are drawn from public design systems so that any reader can check them. Where systems disagree, the disagreement is recorded in `contested` rather than resolved. Confusion pairs are deliberate: they are what the confidence signal is for.

families.navigation: Moves the user to another location or view.
families.text_entry: Accepts free text typed by the user.
families.selection: Sets a value by choosing among predefined options or states.
families.container: A surface that groups and holds other components.
families.indicator: Displays status or information and is not interactive.

Button.what: An interactive control carrying a short verb label that performs an action when activated. Usually a filled, outlined or tinted rectangle with a corner radius; may carry a leading or trailing icon.
Button.not_for: Text that navigates somewhere else instead of acting (Link). A compact removable token (Chip). A control whose whole purpose is showing a value and opening a list (Select).

Link.what: Text that navigates to another page, view or anchor. Typically inline in a sentence or standing alone, distinguished by colour and often an underline, with no filled surface behind it.
Link.not_for: Anything that changes data or submits rather than navigates, even if it is styled as plain text (Button).
Link.contested: A text-only Button and a Link are frequently indistinguishable by appearance alone. Material and Carbon both resolve this by intent, not by looks, which a picture cannot always supply.

Chip.what: A compact interactive token in a pill or rounded rectangle representing an input, filter, selection or attribute. Often carries a dismiss affordance, a leading avatar or icon, or a selected state.
Chip.not_for: A small static count or status marker that cannot be clicked or removed (Badge).
examples: a selectable 'Vegetarian' tag in a filter row

Badge.what: A small non-interactive indicator showing a count, status or short label, frequently attached to the corner of another element such as an icon or avatar.
Badge.not_for: A token the user can select or remove (Chip). Anything clickable.
examples: a red dot with '3' on a bell icon
a green 'Active' status pill in a table row
Badge.contested: Material calls the small count marker a Badge; Polaris uses Badge for status pills that look much like Material's Chips. The visual overlap is real and not a labelling mistake.

Text Input.what: A single-line field that accepts free text typed by the user. A bordered or underlined box, usually with a label above or inside it and often placeholder text.
Text Input.not_for: A field whose purpose is querying, marked by a magnifier icon or 'Search' placeholder (Search Field). A field that opens a list of predefined options instead of accepting typing (Select).

Search Field.what: A text entry control specialised for querying a data set. Recognisable by a magnifier icon, a placeholder naming search, and often a clear affordance or rounded full-width treatment.
Search Field.not_for: Generic free-text entry for a form value (Text Input).
examples: a rounded field with a magnifier and 'Search products'

Select.what: A control that sets a value by opening a list of predefined options. In its collapsed state it shows the current value and a chevron or caret.
Select.not_for: A field the user types into freely (Text Input). A menu opened from a button that performs actions rather than setting a value.

Checkbox.what: A small square control for an independent binary choice, usually with a label beside it. Several may be checked at once within a group. May show a check mark or an indeterminate dash.
Checkbox.not_for: A circular control where exactly one option in the group may be chosen (Radio Button). A sliding track control that applies immediately (Toggle).

Radio Button.what: A small circular control for choosing exactly one option from a mutually exclusive group. Selected state is shown as a filled inner dot.
Radio Button.not_for: Independent choices where more than one may be selected (Checkbox).

Toggle.what: A switch with a track and a sliding thumb that turns a setting on or off, applying the change immediately rather than on submit.
Toggle.not_for: A square control whose value is submitted with a form (Checkbox).
Toggle.contested: Material calls it Switch, Carbon calls it Toggle, and the two systems also differ on whether a Checkbox may ever apply immediately.

Card.what: A bounded surface that groups related content and actions about a single subject, sitting in the normal flow of the page. Usually has a border, elevation or tinted background.
Card.not_for: A surface that floats above the page content and blocks interaction with it (Modal Dialog).
examples: a product tile with image, title, price and an action

Modal Dialog.what: A surface overlaid above the page that requires attention or a decision before the user continues. Usually centred, above a dimmed scrim, with a title, body and one or more actions, and often a close control.
Modal Dialog.not_for: An in-flow grouping surface that does not overlay anything (Card). A small transient label appearing on hover (Tooltip).
examples: a 'Delete this file?' confirmation with Cancel and Delete
Modal Dialog.contested: Judging overlay from a cropped image is often impossible. The surrounding context, not the crop, is what distinguishes these two.

Tabs.what: A row of two or more labels, one of them marked as current by an underline, a filled pill or a heavier weight, which switches the content shown below it. Also called a tab bar. The labels sit on one shared baseline and are usually evenly weighted.
Tabs.not_for: A row of tokens that filter or select without switching a view (Chip). A single isolated label. A row whose items each navigate to a different page rather than swapping content in place.
examples: Overview | Activity | Settings, with Overview underlined
a segmented row of view switchers above a table
Tabs.contested: A row of chips and a tab bar are frequently the same picture: several rounded labels side by side with one highlighted. What separates them is whether the selection switches a view or filters a set, and a crop rarely shows that. Material further splits Tabs from a bottom navigation bar on exactly this question, and the two look alike too.

Other.what: None of the above, or the region does not contain a single identifiable component. Choose this rather than forcing a poor fit.
Other.not_for: A component that does match one of the entries above, even partially.
Other.source: escape hatch, per TypeSafe guidance on including a none-of-the-above option

probes.accepts_typed_text: The region shows a control that the user can type free text into.
probes.has_binary_on_off_state: The region shows a control representing an on/off or checked/unchecked state.
probes.contains_other_components: The region is a surface that holds several smaller components inside it.
probes.is_overlaid_above_content: The region appears to float above other page content, for example over a dimmed backdrop.
probes.is_dismissible: The region shows a control for removing or closing it, such as an × affordance.
